model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route), FCFE basis: AFFO less SBC less equity-funded growth reinvestment

inputs.share_count_basis: Q3 2026 10-Q weighted-average diluted shares 299,994,000 (IRM_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt:2344); FY2026 AFFO guide $1,790M / AFFO-per-share guide $5.97 implies 299.8M, so 300.0M. Held FLAT: SBC is deducted from the flow, and the count has drifted only ~0.6%/yr (296.2M FY2024 -> 300.0M Q3 2026), i.e. award vesting, with no buybacks and no ATM issuance disclosed in Q3 2026 (10-Q line 3507).

debt_memo.treatment: NOT deducted. AFFO is struck after cash interest, so the flow is already to equity; deducting debt again would charge it twice. Leverage enters through (a) interest inside AFFO and (b) the assumption that debt grows with Adjusted EBITDA at a roughly constant ~6x (FY2024 6.1x, FY2025 6.4x, Q3-2026 6.0x on reported debt), which is why only the retained-AFFO share of growth capex is charged to equity.

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement, Stock-based compensation expense 140,280 (thousands) at IRM_Annual_FY2025.txt:4750; 9M 2026 = 115.9M (28.3 + 56.8 + 30.9) -> ~150M FY2026E, 1.9% of revenue. No combined equity-award-tax figure located; cash-flow add-back used.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-06T21:00:03Z regular close (Yahoo chart API regularMarketTime); not an after-hours print
inputs.wacc_rationale: The rate is a COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because AFFO is post-interest. USD flows: 10-year UST ~5.2% + beta ~0.95 x 5.0% ERP = ~10.0%. Beta set above the house net-lease/self-storage REITs (O 0.85 -> 9.5%, PSA 0.75 -> 9.0%) for ~6x leverage, negative book equity, and data-centre development/leasing risk. Same rate in every scenario: risk is carried in the scenario paths and weights, not in a per-scenario premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating lease rent for the ~1,400 leased facilities is inside AFFO as a cash operating cost (IRM's AFFO is struck after rent); lease liabilities are therefore NOT added to the bridge. One treatment, charged once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests immaterial at group level; AFFO guide is IRM's attributable figure.
inputs.notes: MODEL: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity via the component engine (dcf-methods routing: REIT -> AFFO at CoE; IRM is a REIT since 2014 with a large operating services business, but its own primary measure, its dividend policy and its guidance are all AFFO-based, so the whole business is valued on that one post-interest stream rather than split into a sum-of-parts). No prior IRM DCF and no memory entry -- first build. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = total revenue; 'EBITDA margin' = company-defined AFFO / revenue (IRM AFFO adds back stock-based comp, so this is the STREET basis); SBC % deducted separately = HOUSE basis AFFO; D&A 0 and cash tax 0 because AFFO is already after cash taxes and recurring (maintenance) capex; 'capex' = the EQUITY-FUNDED share of growth investment, i.e. retained AFFO (AFFO less dividends), which is what funds the data-centre/ALM growth alongside debt that grows with EBITDA at constant leverage; working capital 0. The flow is thus close to dividends less SBC in the high-growth years and rises toward ~85% of AFFO as growth fades to terminal (terminal reinvestment = g / ~20% incremental levered return on retained equity). FY0 is FY2026E, not FY2025: with Q3 reported and Q4 guided (revenue $7,950-8,020M, AFFO $1,780-1,800M, AFFO/share $5.94-6.00, raised 2026-11-05) the guidance midpoint is ~92% actuals; FY0 AFFO margin = 1,790 / 7,985 = 22.4%, matching FY2024-25 (~22.3-22.4%). AFFO is NOT in the extracted 10-K/10-Q text or Metrics.csv; the guide and the Q3 print ($458.4M, $1.53/sh) come from the Q3-2026 earnings release as recorded in IRM_Analysis.json. OWNER FCF (memo): FY2025 reported FCF = OCF 1,340.0 - capex 2,271.6 = -931.6; less SBC 140.3 = -1,071.9. It is negative because ~$2B/yr of growth capex is debt-funded, which is why an unlevered owner-FCF DCF with net debt deducted is the wrong tool here: it charges every growth dollar to equity while ignoring that ~80% of it is borrowed against the EBITDA it creates. Negative shareholders' equity (-$1,388M Q3 2026) reflects distributions in excess of GAAP earnings after heavy real-estate depreciation -- normal for a mature REIT, not a solvency signal, and irrelevant to an AFFO-based value. Buybacks: none; the flat count is a modelling convention funded by nothing (vesting dilution ~0.6%/yr is the SBC already charged).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FFO (Normalized) 3yr CAGR FY2022 857.8 -> FY2025 1,079.9 (kpis); AFFO itself grew ~16% in FY2026E
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR not computable: book equity turned negative in FY2024 (-503) and FY2025 (-981). GAAP EPS CAGRs (-36.5% / -16.3%) are dominated by real-estate D&A, FX and one-off items and are meaningless for a REIT. Owner FCF is negative every year since FY2021 because of debt-funded growth capex, so FCF CAGRs are undefined. Revenue (10.6-10.7%) and Adjusted EBITDA (12.1%) CAGRs are the usable operating series; FFO (Normalized) 8.0% is the per-equity series selected.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue FY2020 4,147.3 / FY2022 5,103.6 / FY2025 6,901.7; Adjusted EBITDA FY2022 1,827.1 -> FY2025 2,574.0. SBC rose from 56.9 (FY2022, 1.1% of revenue) to 140.3 (FY2025, 2.0%) -- growing much faster than revenue, so an increasing share of reported growth is being paid in stock; it is deducted in the house basis.

base.ebitda_margin_note: AFFO margin (street, SBC added back). FY0 22.4%; +1pp over five years as stabilised data-centre leases (higher margin) outweigh ALM mix dilution and refinancing of ~5% legacy coupons at ~6%.
base.capex_note: Equity-funded growth reinvestment = retained AFFO. FY2027: AFFO ~2,000 less dividends ~1,190 (new $0.993/qtr rate x 300M) = ~810 = ~9% of revenue; trimmed to 8.5%. Glides to 3.5% of revenue (~15% of AFFO) at terminal, i.e. g 3% / ~20% incremental levered return on retained equity.
base.narrative: Guidance-anchored: 2027 revenue +11% as 325-400MW of data-centre capacity energises over 18-24 months against 137MW leased YTD 2026, ALM keeps compounding off ~$850M, and RIM storage holds mid-single-digit price-led growth; growth fades to 3.5% by year 10 as the ~1.4GW build completes.

bull.narrative: AI/hyperscale demand keeps leasing at the Q3-2026 pace (100MW+ quarters), the ~1.4GW target is filled at development yields above IRM's ~6% cost of debt, ALM becomes the multibillion-dollar business management targets, and Insight DXP lifts digital recurring revenue; AFFO margin expands ~2.6pp on data-centre mix.

bear.narrative: Sub-scale against Equinix/Digital Realty: hyperscale leasing slows after the already-signed capacity energises, new capacity leases at thinner yields, and the ~$18B debt stack reprices from ~5% to 6%+ as it refinances, compressing AFFO margin ~1.4pp; ALM and digitisation projects soften in a downturn and RIM volumes drift lower, leaving growth near inflation.

scenario_narratives.base: Guidance-anchored: data-centre energisation (325-400MW over 18-24 months) and ALM carry 2027 revenue growth of ~11%, fading to 3.5% by year 10; AFFO margin edges up ~1pp; IRM keeps retaining ~40% of AFFO and borrowing against EBITDA growth at ~6x to fund the build.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI/hyperscale leasing stays at the Q3-2026 pace, the ~1.4GW target fills at yields well above debt cost, ALM scales to a multibillion-dollar line and digital lifts mix; growth stays double-digit for five years and AFFO margin reaches 25%.
scenario_narratives.bear: IRM loses the power/land/tenant race to better-capitalised specialists after the signed pipeline energises, refinancing lifts interest cost on ~$18B of debt, ALM/digital soften in a downturn and records volumes erode: growth falls to inflation and AFFO margin compresses to 21%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25% because the growth plan depends on continuous debt-market access at ~6x leverage with negative book equity, and the data-centre thesis rests on a sub-scale challenger winning against Equinix/DLR. Bull trimmed to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right (leasing pace, development yields, ALM scaling and benign rates). Base 50% reflects full-year guidance raised again on 2026-11-05 and 137MW already leased YTD.

valuation_philosophy.summary: IRM is valued as what it is to an equity holder: a post-interest AFFO stream, less the stock-based comp that IRM's AFFO adds back, less the retained AFFO that funds growth alongside EBITDA-backed borrowing, capitalised at a 10% cost of equity. Debt is not deducted again. The street basis (SBC treated as non-cash) is reported as a memo.
key_risks_to_valuation: Leverage assumption: the model lets debt grow with Adjusted EBITDA at ~6x; if IRM has to de-lever toward its stated 4.5-5.5x net lease-adjusted range, more growth must be funded by retained AFFO or equity issuance and the per-share flow falls.
Data-centre development yields: growth is only value-creating if stabilised yields stay well above IRM's ~6% marginal cost of debt.
AFFO definition: AFFO is company-defined and taken from the earnings release, not the 10-Q; it excludes growth capex and adds back SBC (the house basis deducts SBC).
Interest-rate sensitivity: a 1pp move in the cost of equity moves value ~15%; refinancing ~$18B at higher coupons compresses AFFO margin (bear path).
Terminal value is the majority of value; Gordon binds below the 18x cap in every scenario.
